# A sum of two limbs rounded down

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `add_down_1` · proved for finite operands · proved for infinite and NaN operands · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

$a + b$ rounded to a number of `T`:

$$r = \mathrm{RD}(a + b).$$

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of [`add_down_entry`](add_down_entry.md), [`sub_down_1`](sub_down_1.md), [`interval_add_1`](interval_add_1.md).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $r = \mathrm{RD}(a + b)$: the largest number of the format not above $a + b$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `add_down_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/DirectedSum.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/DirectedSum.v), against `add_down_1_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions add_down_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition add_down_1_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (2 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall a b : R,
  fmt emin prec a ->
  fmt emin prec b ->
  let r := add_down_1 emin prec tie_even a b in
  fmt emin prec r /\
  r = RD emin prec (a + b).
```

## Infinite and NaN operands

The statement above is about finite operands. The claims also say what the kernel returns when its operands may be infinite or NaN. That statement requires:

- $a$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.
- $b$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.

and then:

- If every operand is finite: $r$ is the largest number of `T` not above $a + b$, or $-\infty$ when $a + b < -\Omega$ ($\Omega$ is the largest finite number of `T`).
- If an operand is infinite or NaN: $r = a + b$, as `T` computes it.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

**Status of this statement:** proved. Rocq checks the theorem `add_down_1_ieee_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeDirected.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeDirected.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions add_down_1_ieee_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proofs of `add_down_1_correct` and `add_down_1_ieee_correct` depend on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the rounded sum and the sign of its exact error (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/add_down_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/add_down_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`two_sum_ord`](two_sum_ord.md).

```
# RD(a + b), the largest number of the format not above the exact sum, for every pair of finite
# numbers (milestone2.md, "Rounding a sum down and up"): the rounded sum, one step down when its
# exact error is negative. two_sum_ord's error term is the exact error, so its sign decides. At an
# overflow the error term is the infinity of the opposite sign, which chooses the right
# neighbor: Omega for a sum that overflows upward, -inf for one that overflows downward (the
# format with overflow). An infinite or NaN operand gives the sum of IEEE 754.

(s, e) = two_sum_ord(a, b)
n      = lt(e, 0)
p      = pred(s)
r      = select(n, p, s)
```

## Measured

The stored brute-force runs of this kernel's code: the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound. A run is shown only if it ran the code the kernel has now: its generated C++ (scalar and packed, every kernel it calls inlined, with the functions it calls; comments left out) must be the same at the commit of the run, as the fingerprints in [`results/brute-code.json`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/results/brute-code.json) show ([How to read a page](reading.md#what-the-measured-numbers-are)).

**Milestone 2**: the runs of commit `5f597fb`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#add_down_1)).
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 103 500 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 103 500 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 6 416 404 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements of the statement on infinite and NaN operands.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
